related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests using literal terms including `xgboost-cpu`, `xgboost`, the reported AttributeError, and `RECORD`; conceptual terms including same module, top-level import, overlapping/shared files, package override, file ownership, namespace package, uninstall, and incomplete installation; and fix-oriented terms covering collision warnings, preview conflict detection, RECORD-aware uninstall, and environment repair. Inspected candidate comments and their referenced canonical discussions and implementation history. astral-sh/uv#16468 was ruled out because it concerns remove/re-add with a missing RECORD rather than two distributions sharing paths. astral-sh/uv#21968 concerns unexplained missing NCCL files after a possibly full filesystem, without an overlapping-distribution uninstall. astral-sh/uv#17645 is another instance of the same overlap pattern, but the selected trackers are more canonical.

type_reason: The two substantive behaviors are already tracked: astral-sh/uv#15357 covers detecting conflicting module providers, while astral-sh/uv#15238 covers deletion of shared files during uninstall. The xgboost/xgboost-cpu example is a new reproduction of those existing problems, not a regression of a completed fix; collision warnings remain intentionally preview-only, and the proposed uninstall fix in astral-sh/uv#19430 was not merged.
summary: astral-sh/uv#15357 is the canonical collision-detection tracker, and astral-sh/uv#15238 tracks the same shared-file uninstall corruption. Historical pull requests explain why warnings remain preview-only and why the direct RECORD-preservation fix was rejected.
draft_response:
Thanks for the concrete reproduction. This is the same overlapping-distribution problem tracked in astral-sh/uv#15357, with the uninstall failure specifically tracked in astral-sh/uv#15238.

`xgboost` and `xgboost-cpu` are distinct distribution names to the resolver, and their metadata does not declare that they conflict or substitute for one another. Their wheels nevertheless write overlapping paths in the `xgboost` import package. Removing `xgboost` deletes paths listed in its `RECORD`, including paths still needed by `xgboost-cpu`, leaving the latter's dist-info present but its module incomplete.

`uv sync --reinstall-package xgboost-cpu` should restore the affected environment. Conflict detection currently remains a preview feature because some packages intentionally overlap, and it is most reliable when both distributions are installed in the same operation. We should centralize further work in astral-sh/uv#15357 and astral-sh/uv#15238, so this can be closed as a duplicate.
